title: Construct the complete selected P104 two-rate guard frontier
body:
The exact selected PR6030 word now has a complete two-rate precision schedule: 15 native / 16 scalar guard bits, or 14 native / 17 scalar bits. These are the only Pareto corners of the retained causal sufficient rule over all nonnegative integer guards. The first saves 3,453 guard bits across operation occurrences (363,488 → 360,035); the second allows four times the uniform-16 native defect. The README gives the exact positive-tariff switch between them.

All 22,803 events, 770 public inputs, 29 owned fields and actual-input defect feedback are included. Both schedules keep final public Hilbert error below B and every ideal-plus-error prefix below 1024B. Adding t bits to both classes gives final error below B·2^-t. Exact COPY/INIT/owned reset and the inherited unitary common-chart contract remain premises. Failure of the sufficient rule is not a physical precision lower bound.

Verification: all ideal endpoint rows; five finite frontier corners and two exact-class tail exclusions; both full signed transposes; complete equality with the unchanged uniform evaluator; 36 independent rational fixtures; nine rejection controls. CPython 3.12.14 normal/optimized registered replay, byte/mode checks, official export and read-only Git-free/empty-PATH normal/optimized replay pass at `7edc16a02d7244847432af3c2d97443fb4146141`. Hosted CI is pending. The optional full-history preflight was not run in this shallow checkout; all live sources come from the immediate main parent and are included in the cold export.

Reproduce: `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-two-rate-guards`.

No new kappa, runtime saving, physical backend or selected-frontier change. The next task is a completed native/scalar backend with a real precision price, range, conversion and cleanup bill. Concurrent PR6473 proves the separate PR6398 mixed caller error contract; its source and boundary differ, and no automatic composition is claimed.

[Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5600#discussioncomment-19363163). Main, handoffs and related open work were refreshed before submission. Credit DreamingOfClouds/PR6030 and PR5907; Ali Romman's retained causal and signed-row method; Adam Gall, ywz65, Mason Hale, Pierre-Loic Doulcet and the complete P104/native/compiler lineage. Prepared for Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents. Apache-2.0.
